verdict.rationale: Better Stack documents several user-configured automations that run unattended: monitors that check URLs on a recurring interval and automatically create incidents and alert on-call, escalation policies that keep escalating until someone acknowledges, and incident triggers that post todo lists and route responders. Its AI side also produces fix pull requests and automated post-mortems. However, these automations are tied to monitoring and incident workflows rather than being general-purpose, and the AI SRE explicitly 'never takes any automated actions without your approval,' which limits agentic autonomy. Missing for 10: a general-purpose automation/workflow builder, autonomous AI agent actions without approval gating, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: An HTTP status code monitor checks your URLs every X seconds for an HTTP success status code (2XX). If the URL doesn't return this code, the monitor creates an Incident and alerts the current on-call person.
It defines who will be alerted and in what order, continuing until the incident is acknowledged.
Post a todo list when a new incident is triggered. Route the incident to the right responder.
Got an exception? Get a pull request with a suggested fix waiting for you in GitHub.
Get an automated post-mortem based on the incident timeline and Slack.
The AI SRE suggests hypotheses but never takes any automated actions without your approval.
